title: Graph and Simplicial Complex Prediction Gaussian Process via Hodgelet Representations
claim: Graphs encode only pairwise relations, while simplicial complexes add higher-order filled cells, motivating richer topological structure.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, filled blue triangles mark the contrast
description: Two side-by-side panels show the same kind of network structure. Panel (a), captioned 'Simplicial 1-complex (graph)', shows orange circular vertices joined by black edges. It has a few triangle-shaped cycles, but they are empty, plus several dangling leaf nodes. Panel (b), captioned 'Simplicial 2-complex', is a similar network of orange vertices and black edges. Several of its triangles are filled with blue gradient shading, which marks 2-simplices. The filled triangles cluster on the left and on the right, and a hollow quadrilateral loop is left between them. There is no math notation and no arrows. The eye goes first to the saturated blue triangles in the right panel. These contrast with the plain line-only graph on the left.
caption: Orange vertices are $0$-simplices, black edges are $1$-simplices, and blue triangles are $2$-simplices.
abstract: Predicting labels for graph-structured data is crucial in many scientific applications. Recently, Gaussian processes with graph-level inputs have been proposed as flexible non-parametric models for classification tasks. In this work, we extend this framework to regression tasks and to simplicial complexes, enabling the modelling of attributes defined on edges and higher-order simplices. Drawing on Hodge theory, we construct representations based on the Hodge decomposition, allowing the model to distinguish between exact, co-exact, and harmonic signal components. We introduce Hodgelet representations as rich, learnable topological descriptors of simplicial complexes and show that our framework improves predictive performance across a range of applications. Our work broadens the applicability of Gaussian processes to prediction tasks at the graph and simplicial-complex levels.
